title: FIGMA - Party role (Assign a new party role)
walkthroughSteps: Navigate to /fnol/parties: a policy is pre-selected so the step doesn't redirect to search. Add parties with Add additional parties if the list is empty

walkthroughSteps.title: Party role
walkthroughSteps.body: Every party row has an actions menu with View details, Edit role, and Remove. For a default party (client, broker or insured from the policy) the middle item is Edit reference number instead, because its role can't be changed.
walkthroughSteps.expectedAfterClick: Opens the row's action menu. Edit role opens a single-choice list of claim roles and the Reference number field.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every party row has an Edit role action
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: Each party on the FNOL Parties step has an actions menu including **Edit role**, for assigning or changing that party's role. Default parties show **Edit reference number** instead (see AC-03).

setup.description: Seed a selected policy so /fnol/parties doesn't redirect to /fnol/search

preconditions.text: At least one party row with an Edit role action is visible

expectedUI.description: Party row actions menu with Edit role
visualCues: Kebab action button per party row
Menu includes View details, Edit role (or Edit reference number for a default party), Remove

howToTest.trigger: Click a party row's actions kebab
howToTest.expectedResult: Menu opens with Edit role available

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A party has exactly one claim role, picked from the Jira list
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: **Edit role** shows the claim roles as a single-choice list (radio buttons): **Claimant, Claims Third Party, Lawyer, Loss Adjuster, Other**. Only one can be picked, as the Jira story says ("only single Claim role for a specific party"). The table column is called **Party role**.

setup.description: Seed a selected policy so /fnol/parties doesn't redirect to /fnol/search

preconditions.text: A non-default party row (for example a claimant) is visible
Edit role dialog shows five radio options

visualCues: Five radio options in Jira order

howToTest.trigger: Open a claimant's row menu, click Edit role, pick Lawyer, Save
howToTest.expectedResult: The row's Party role reads Lawyer

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The role of a default party can't be changed
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: Default parties come from the policy (Client, Broker, Insured). Their role is shown as read-only text with the line "This party comes from the policy, so its role can't be changed." Only the reference number can be edited.

setup.description: Seed a selected policy so /fnol/parties doesn't redirect to /fnol/search

preconditions.text: A default party row (for example the client) is visible
Dialog shows the role as text, not as options

expectedUI.description: Edit reference number dialog for a default party
visualCues: Party role shown as plain text

howToTest.trigger: Open the client's row menu, click Edit reference number
howToTest.expectedResult: Role is read-only; only Reference number can be changed

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A Reference number column sits after the Party role column
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: The parties table has a **Reference number** column right after **Party role**. The handler can add or change it at any time from the row menu. Letters and numbers only, up to 35 characters. An empty value shows a dash. **NOTE:** the 35-character limit is a prototype choice; Jira gives no length.
